findings.issue: Wave 3 sequencing violation: Task 8 (Settings popup controls) and Task 9 (Migrate existing E2E locators) run in parallel, but Task 8 breaks exactly what Task 9 fixes. Task 8 turns popup row group names into input values inside `src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte`; Task 9 migrates the popup row locators in `tests/e2e/0006-group-visibility.spec.ts` and helpers. Task 8's own verify command is `npx playwright test tests/e2e/0006-group-visibility.spec.ts` — it cannot pass until Task 9 has landed. Task 9's verify (`npx playwright test`) is symmetrically unstable while Task 8 mutates the popup. The Risks table already states the intended order explicitly ("Task 9 migrates those locators before new scenarios are written"), but the wave layout does not encode it.
findings.fix: Move Task 9 into Wave 2 (its locator migration depends only on the `data-group-container` wrapper from Task 7 and on `data-group-id`, both available then), or split Wave 3 so Task 9 runs first and Task 8 moves to Wave 4 alongside Task 10.

findings.issue: Task 5 description embeds a technical decision with rationale: "A renamed group also shows a neutral hint when empty, because the original hint describes a meaning the user has replaced." Decision-marker "because" — rationale belongs in the Decisions section.
findings.fix: Add a Decision entry (e.g. "Renamed groups fall back to a neutral empty-state hint") with Decision / Rationale / Alternatives considered, and reduce the task line to the scope statement: "A renamed group also shows the neutral empty hint."

findings.issue: Task 9 description embeds rationale: "Popup row locators break regardless of renaming because the name becomes an input value, so they must move too." This duplicates the Risks-table row on the same subject and carries a "because" rationale in a task description.
findings.fix: Keep only scope in the task ("Popup row locators move to group identifiers as well") and leave the reasoning in Risks / Decisions.

findings.issue: Task 4 description restates Decision 5's rationale nearly verbatim: "This is the most branch-heavy logic in the feature and is verified in isolation" vs Decision 5 "This is the most branch-heavy new logic in the feature. Verifying it only through browser scenarios would be slow and unreliable." Duplication between Decisions and a task description.
findings.fix: Drop the second sentence from Task 4; the rationale is already fully stated in Decision 5.

findings.issue: Task 2 description carries procedural/decision content rather than scope: "Verify the runtime before anything else — if Node is below the required version, stop and report rather than working around it." This is Decision 7's policy restated as an execution instruction inside the task.
findings.fix: Reduce Task 2 to scope ("Pin the required Node version in the repo and bring the board-layout test into the collected test set") and keep the stop-on-mismatch policy in Decision 7 / Risks, where it already appears.

findings.issue: Task 5 claims to cover title display in "the board settings list", and the Architecture section lists `BoardSettingsPopup` as a title-resolution site — but `src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte` is not in Task 5's Files to modify. It appears only in Task 8, one wave later. The stated scope of Task 5 cannot be delivered from its declared file set.
findings.fix: Either remove "the board settings list" from Task 5's description (leaving that surface entirely to Task 8), or add `src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte` to Task 5 — but not both, since Task 8 also modifies that file and a same-file split across waves must be explicit.

findings.issue: Every `code-writing` task (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) omits `dev-security-auditor`, and Task 2 (`infrastructure-setup`) omits it too. The catalog default reviewer set for both skills includes it. This matters most for Task 8, which introduces a free-text user-editable group name, and Task 5, which renders that value across five components — CLAUDE.md's no-`{@html}` rule is exactly the kind of constraint that reviewer checks.
findings.fix: Add `dev-security-auditor` at least to Tasks 5, 6 and 8 (user input entering the store and being rendered), or state explicitly in the tech-spec why the default set is reduced for this feature.

findings.issue: Project Knowledge is absent — `.claude/skills/project-knowledge/references/architecture.md` and `patterns.md` do not exist in this repository. Standards compliance (directory structure, component naming, file organization) could not be verified against a documented baseline; the proposed paths were only checked against the conventions in CLAUDE.md, where they are consistent (`src/ui/*.svelte`, `tests/unit/*.test.ts`, `tm-` CSS prefix implied by `src/styles.css` edits).
findings.fix: Optional: create the project-knowledge references so future tech-specs can be validated against a real architecture baseline instead of CLAUDE.md alone.

findings.issue: Task 10's description is a single sentence packing six distinct E2E scenarios plus a rationale clause ("including a collapsible group, where the drag binding is most fragile"). It reads as a test plan rather than a scope statement, and the scenario list already exists verbatim in Testing Strategy → E2E tests.
findings.fix: Shorten to scope: "Cover the feature end to end per the E2E scenarios in Testing Strategy, including drag & drop between reordered groups without reload."

findings.issue: Task 4 lists `src/data/types.ts` in Files to read, but Task 1 modifies that same file in the same wave (Wave 1). Task 4 may read a version of the file that does not yet contain `Board.groupOrder`.
findings.fix: Confirm Task 4 only needs the pre-existing `GroupId` union (in which case note that), or move Task 4 to Wave 2.

findings.issue: Task 6 (Wave 2) extends `BoardHeader.svelte` to carry titles and order from the popup's `onSave`, but the popup only starts emitting them in Task 8 (Wave 3). The plumbing is verified by `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` before any producer exists, so the persistence path is not functionally exercisable within its own wave.
findings.fix: Acceptable as consumer-first plumbing, but state the ordering explicitly in the task ("popup emits these in Task 8") so the executing agent does not attempt an end-to-end check it cannot perform.

summary: Template compliance is strong: frontmatter is complete and valid (created 2026-08-06, status draft, branch feature/group-customization, size L), all template sections including Backward Compatibility are present and non-empty, all 10 Decisions carry Decision + Rationale + Alternatives, Risks is a proper table with realistic non-generic entries, Agent Verification Plan is filled with concrete bash commands per task, Final Wave contains Pre-deploy QA with skill pre-deploy-qa and no reviewers, 11 tasks (<= 15), all skills and reviewers exist in the catalog and on disk, and the document is entirely time-free with no line-number references, no AC blocks and no TDD anchors inside tasks. One critical issue blocks approval: Wave 3 puts Task 8 and Task 9 in parallel although Task 8's verification depends on Task 9's locator migration — an ordering the Risks table already assumes but the wave layout does not encode. Five major findings concern decision rationale leaking into task descriptions (Tasks 2, 4, 5, 9) and a scope/file-set mismatch in Task 5.
